payload.task_text:
I need to analyze our product reviews by combining external review data with our internal store reviews. There is a review aggregation site at http://localhost:30307 with aggregated ratings from multiple platforms. Please visit and extract all the product review data.

The aggregation table lists exactly 8 products: Wireless Headphones, Smart Watch, Bluetooth Speaker, USB-C Hub, Webcam HD, Mechanical Keyboard, Gaming Mouse, and Laptop Stand. The External_Reviews sheet must contain one row for each of these 8 products.

Then check our online store (WooCommerce) for our internal product reviews, ratings, and sales data, and save them into internal_reviews.json.

Write and run a Python script called review_analyzer.py that reads external_reviews.json and internal_reviews.json (create both), compares ratings, identifies discrepancies, and outputs review_insights.json.

Create an Excel file called Review_Analysis_Report.xlsx with two sheets. The first sheet External_Reviews should have columns Product, External_Rating, Review_Count, Sentiment, and Common_Complaint. The second sheet Review_Summary should have Metric and Value columns with Total_Products_Reviewed, Avg_External_Rating (round to 2 decimals), Positive_Products, and Needs_Attention (count of Negative or Mixed sentiment products). Write all numeric values in the Excel file as literal numbers, not Excel formulas.

Also create a page in the team knowledge base titled "Product Review Tracker" with a summary of products needing attention and their common complaints.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete this bounded eight-product job directly in the main agent and use native parallel calls after each input key set is frozen. Resolve the runtime workspace root first. Read the aggregation site and freeze exactly these eight rows and spellings: `Wireless Headphones`, `Smart Watch`, `Bluetooth Speaker`, `USB-C Hub`, `Webcam HD`, `Mechanical Keyboard`, `Gaming Mouse`, and `Laptop Stand`, including each external rating, review count, sentiment, and common complaint. Write and read back `external_reviews.json` at that resolved root with exactly one row per listed product.

Next issue the eight independent `woo_products_list(search=<exact product name>, perPage=100, page=1)` calls in one native-parallel response. Resolve each name to exactly one product ID using an exact normalized-name match; if a search is ambiguous or missing, stop for that product rather than guessing. With the eight IDs frozen, issue the eight independent `woo_products_get(productId=<frozen ID>)` calls and the eight independent paginated `woo_products_reviews_list(productId=<frozen ID>, status="approved", perPage=100, page=<n>)` streams using native parallel calls. Continue a review stream until a short or empty page, deduplicate by review ID, and record page counts. Build `internal_reviews.json` at the resolved root keyed by the same eight product names with exact product ID, rating/rating count, total sales fields exposed by the product record, approved review rows, and pagination/duplicate controls; do not enumerate the unrelated WooCommerce catalog.

Create `review_analyzer.py` at the resolved root as the sole computation implementation. It must read only the two JSON inputs, compare the frozen product rows, identify rating discrepancies and attention products, and write `review_insights.json` beside them; run it once, then read back all three JSON files and require exactly-once coverage of the eight names. From that canonical result, act as the sole writer of `Review_Analysis_Report.xlsx` at the resolved root: `External_Reviews` must contain the exact requested five columns and eight rows, while `Review_Summary` must contain literal numeric values for `Total_Products_Reviewed`, `Avg_External_Rating` rounded to two decimals, `Positive_Products`, and `Needs_Attention`, where the last metric counts only `Negative` or `Mixed` rows. Read both sheets back and reconcile them to the JSON output.

Finally search the team knowledge base for the exact title `Product Review Tracker`; update the exact existing task page if present, otherwise create it once. Include the source-backed products whose sentiment is `Negative` or `Mixed` and each corresponding common complaint, then read the page back. Do not dispatch sub-agents or verification work; any original requirement not stated here remains the main agent's responsibility.

nodes.text:
You are gathering read-only data from a WooCommerce store via the granted `mcp__woocommerce__*` tools. Your job is ONLY to collect and report data — do not attempt to write any files.

## Context
I am building a product-review analysis that compares an external review aggregation site (which lists 8 generic product types) against our internal WooCommerce store data. I need a complete, compact inventory of the WooCommerce catalog, plus the product reviews, so I can map each of the 8 generic product types to the correct store product.

The 8 generic product types are:
1. Wireless Headphones
2. Smart Watch
3. Bluetooth Speaker
4. USB-C Hub
5. Webcam HD
6. Mechanical Keyboard
7. Gaming Mouse
8. Laptop Stand

## What I already know
- The catalog contains roughly 82 products (IDs roughly 1-82), sourced from a Kaggle Amazon 2023 dataset. Product names are long Amazon-style titles.
- Categories that exist: Audio (15), Cameras (10), Electronics (30), Headphones (10), Home Appliances (8), Speakers (5), TV & Home Theater (13), Watches (6).
- Product reviews exist (I saw review IDs 297-396 covering product_ids 59-82).
- IMPORTANT: calling `mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_list` with perPage=100 returns ~190KB and gets TRUNCATED/capped (invalid JSON with unescaped quotes in names like `Samsung 1m 09cm (43") Smart Monitor`). To avoid this you MUST page with a small page size, e.g. perPage=20 (roughly 5 pages). Verify you have covered every product (keep paging until an empty array or repeated IDs).

## Task 1 — Full compact product inventory
Page through `mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_list` (perPage=20, page=1,2,3,...) and build a compact array with EXACTLY these fields for every product:
- id
- name
- average_rating (as number)
- rating_count
- total_sales
- price
- categories (just category names, comma-joined)
- tags (just tag names, comma-joined)

Report this as a JSON array in your final answer. Keep it compact — no descriptions, no images, no meta_data.

## Task 2 — Reviews
Page through `mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_reviews_list` with status="approved" and perPage=100 (page=1,2,...) until exhausted. Report:
(a) the total number of reviews,
(b) a mapping of product_id -> number of reviews,
(c) for the products you identify as best matches in Task 3 below, the full list of their reviews with fields: id, product_id, reviewer, rating, verified, date_created, and the review text (truncate the review text to at most 250 characters).

## Task 3 — Matching
For EACH of the 8 generic product types above, identify the best-matching WooCommerce product(s). Use the product name semantics (and tags/categories as supporting evidence). Report:
- the product type,
- your chosen best match (id + name + average_rating + rating_count + total_sales),
- ALL other plausible candidate matches (id + name), so I can verify your choice.

If a product type has NO plausible match in the catalog, say so explicitly and list the closest 2-3 products in that area.

## Constraints
- Read-only. Do not create/update/delete anything in WooCommerce.
- Do not write files.
- Be precise with numbers — copy them exactly as returned.
- If a tool call fails, note it and continue with what works.

## Deliverable
A single final report containing: (1) the compact product inventory JSON array, (2) review stats and the per-matched-product reviews, (3) the matching table with best match + alternatives. Make the numbers unambiguous so I can use them directly.
Inventory WooCommerce catalog

Create a page in our team knowledge base (Notion) using the granted `mcp__notion__*` tools. Do not use any other write tools.

## Goal
Create a Notion page titled **"Product Review Tracker"** containing a summary of products needing attention and their common complaints.

## Where to create it
- The team knowledge base is the Notion page **"Team Notes"** (page id `noise-review-001`, it is the only page in the workspace and it is currently empty).
- Create the new page as a **child of "Team Notes"** (parent = `{"page_id": "noise-review-001"}`, or `{"type":"page_id","page_id":"noise-review-001"}`).
- If — and only if — creating it as a child of "Team Notes" fails, fall back to creating it at the workspace root (parent = `{"type":"workspace","workspace":true}`).
- Do NOT modify or delete the existing "Team Notes" page itself.

## Important technical note
When calling `mcp__notion__API-post-page`, the `parent` and `properties` arguments must be passed as actual JSON objects (not JSON strings). If you hit an error like "/parent must be object" or "/properties must be object", the arguments were sent as strings — retry passing them as real nested objects. If `API-post-page` still refuses the arguments after several attempts, report exactly what you tried and what error you got, rather than giving up silently.

## Exact page content to create
Title: `Product Review Tracker`
Icon: 📊 (optional, add if accepted)

Add these blocks in order:

1. Paragraph: `External review data from ReviewHub (50+ platforms, Q1 2026) was compared against our internal WooCommerce store ratings, reviews and sales data. Of the 8 products tracked, 2 have Negative or Mixed external sentiment and need attention. Average external rating is 4.10 / 5.`

2. Heading 1: `Products Needing Attention`

3. Paragraph: `The 2 products below have Negative or Mixed external sentiment and are the priority follow-up items, ranked by review volume (impact).`

4. A table (6 columns, header row + 2 data rows):
   - Header: Product | Sentiment | External Rating | External Reviews | Common Complaint | Internal Rating
   - Row 1: Smart Watch | Mixed | 3.8 / 5 | 890 | Screen durability | 4.00 / 5
   - Row 2: USB-C Hub | Negative | 3.2 / 5 | 560 | Compatibility issues | 4.00 / 5

5. Heading 2: `1. Smart Watch — Mixed sentiment (890 external reviews)` with these bullets:
   - `Common complaint: Screen durability.`
   - `External rating 3.8 / 5 (Mixed) across 890 reviews — the second-lowest of the 8 tracked products.`
   - `Internal match: "boAt Wave Call Smart Watch" (product ID 25) — 4.00 / 5 from 5 reviews, 170 units sold.`
   - `Rating gap +0.20 (+5.26%) — On Track band, inside the 0.5 discrepancy threshold.`
   - `Action: monitor closely. Screen durability is the dominant external complaint and our small internal sample (5 reviews) may not yet surface it.`

6. Heading 2: `2. USB-C Hub — Negative sentiment and the only rating discrepancy` with these bullets:
   - `Common complaint: Compatibility issues.`
   - `External rating 3.2 / 5 (Negative) across 560 reviews — the lowest of the 8 tracked products.`
   - `Internal match: "ZEBRONICS Zeb-100HB 4 Ports USB Hub" (product ID 13) — 4.00 / 5 from 3 reviews, 166 units sold.`
   - `Rating gap +0.80 (+25.0%) — Critical band and the only product exceeding the 0.5 rating discrepancy threshold.`
   - `Action: immediate attention required. Externally reported compatibility issues are not reflected in our internal ratings; verify the compatibility complaint and consider sourcing a true USB-C hub (our current item is a USB-A hub).`

7. Heading 1: `Rating Discrepancies (> 0.5)` followed by paragraph: `Applying the >0.5 rating discrepancy rule, 1 of the 5 products carried internally is flagged: USB-C Hub (internal 4.00 vs external 3.20, +0.80). All other matched products are within 0.4 of their external rating.`

8. Heading 1: `Full Product Review Summary` followed by a table (6 columns, header + 8 data rows):
   - Header: Product | External Rating | Review Count | Sentiment | Common Complaint | Status
   - Wireless Headphones | 4.2 | 1250 | Positive | Battery life | OK
   - Smart Watch | 3.8 | 890 | Mixed | Screen durability | Needs attention
   - Bluetooth Speaker | 4.5 | 2100 | Positive | None major | OK
   - USB-C Hub | 3.2 | 560 | Negative | Compatibility issues | Needs attention
   - Webcam HD | 4.0 | 780 | Positive | Low light performance | OK
   - Mechanical Keyboard | 4.7 | 1800 | Very Positive | None | OK
   - Gaming Mouse | 4.3 | 950 | Positive | Cable quality | OK
   - Laptop Stand | 4.1 | 420 | Positive | Stability | OK

   If Notion tables are awkward, you may substitute a clean bulleted list with the same information, but keep every value.

9. Heading 1: `Key Metrics` with these bullets:
   - `Total products reviewed: 8`
   - `Average external rating: 4.10 / 5`
   - `Products with positive sentiment: 6 of 8 (includes one "Very Positive")`
   - `Products needing attention: 2 of 8 (Negative or Mixed sentiment)`
   - `Total external reviews across the 8 products: 8,750`

10. Heading 1: `Data Sources & Method` with these bullets:
   - `External: ReviewHub aggregated product ratings (50+ platforms), Q1 2026.`
   - `Internal: WooCommerce store — 82 products, 396 approved reviews, average rating 4.62 across all products.`
   - `Each external product was matched to the closest store product; 5 of the 8 have an internal counterpart. Webcam HD, Mechanical Keyboard and Gaming Mouse are not carried in our catalogue, so no internal comparison is available for them.`
   - `A product is flagged as a discrepancy when |internal − external| > 0.5; gap percentages are banded as Critical (>20%), Warning (10–20%) and On Track (<10%).`
   - `Full details: review_insights.json, Review_Analysis_Report.xlsx (sheets External_Reviews and Review_Summary).`

## Deliverable (report back)
- Whether the page was created, and under which parent (child of "Team Notes" or workspace root).
- The new page's id and URL.
- The page title as it now reads.
- A short confirmation that both tables and all sections were created (or exactly which parts failed and why).
- Do not create more than one page. If you accidentally create a duplicate, delete the extra one with `API-delete-a-block`.
